newsitem.title: TURKEY: Fighting reported on Iraqi Kurdish front.
newsitem.headline: Fighting reported on Iraqi Kurdish front.

text.p: Peshmerga guerrillas of the Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP), backed by Iraqi government tanks and artillery, resumed their assault on the strategic town of Degala on Sunday, a rival Kurdish faction said.
The Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK) reported fierce fighting along its defensive line at Degala, guarding the main road to its stronghold of Sulaimaniya.
"The objective of the attack is to break through (PUK) defensive lines toward the city of Koi Sanjak, home to 80,000 people," the PUK said in a statement.
"We call on the U.S. and its coalition partners to intervene urgently to halt the Iraqi aggression and end this onslaught against the Kurdish people," the group said.
KDP radio confirmed heavy fighting along the front, saying its forces had surrounded their rivals and calling on them to surrender.
Iraq joined the fighting in its rebel north a week ago on the side of the Kurdistan Democratic Party to kick the PUK out of the main northern Iraqi Kurdish city of Arbil.

Residents of Sulaimaniya have largely pinned their hopes on Washington, which retaliated for Iraqi President Saddam Hussein's thrust into northern Iraq by sending two volleys of cruise missiles into southern Iraq last week.
Sulaimaniya, 120 km (72 miles) south of Arbil, is the last major northern Iraqi settlement still in PUK hands. The KDP and PUK have been fighting for decades.
